question.leadin: This document originally contained 39 separate provisions, though only 10 were ratified.
question.text: Name this set of 10 amendments added to the U.S. Constitution in 1791.
question.clue: This document ratified in the Massachusetts Compromise was derided as a "parchment barrier" by James Madison, and William Douglas argued that its penumbra protected a "zone of privacy" in Griswold v Connecticut.

swap.text: This battle of the Texas Revolution resulted in the deaths of James Bowie and Davy Crockett. The site of this battle was a Spanish mission in San Antonio founded by Fray Antonio de Olivares.
swap.clue: During this battle, a letter was addressed to "all Americans in the World" and signed "Victory or Death" by losing commander William Barret Travis.

question.leadin: The Federalist Papers were authored by Alexander Hamilton, John Jay, and this man.
question.text: Name this fourth president of the United States, whose wife Dolley famously saved a portrait of George Washington from a British attack on the White House.
question.clue: A portrait of George Washington was purportedly rescued by this president's wife as they both fled the burning of the White House.

swap.leadin: Identify the following Secretaries of State.
swap.text: This politician from Massachusetts was also a successful orator and lawyer; he signed a treaty with Ashburton to resolve a border dispute in Maine with Canada as Secretary of State for William Henry Harrison and John Tyler.
swap.clue: This man declared that "there are those who love it" while defending his alma mater in Dartmouth College v. Woodward, and he lost his Senate seat after he defended the Compromise of 1850 in his Seventh of March speech.

question.leadin: Answer the following about a supreme court chief justice.
question.text: This man was the first Chief Justice of the United States. He later retired from the position to become the governor of New York.
question.clue: The founder of the New York Manumission Society, this man, who is not Alexander Hamilton, had a Jeffersonian cry made against him that said "Damn everyone that won't damn" this man.

swap.leadin: William Strickland built this institution in a Greek Revival style for its President, Nicholas Biddle.
swap.text: Name this national institution that was destroyed by the Distribution Act of 1836, which forced currency to be only gold and silver.
swap.answer: Second Bank of the United States
swap.clue: An opponent of this organization was the first cabinet appointee to be rejected by the Senate, after his recess appointment expired.

question.text: Some of the Cherokee signed this treaty in 1835, although none of their chiefs agreed. This treaty, named after the last Cherokee capital, ceded their land to the US.
question.clue: It was steadfastly opposed by John Ross, and the group that was involved in it, known as the "Ridge Party," was in violation of the law.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about a conflict in which the U.S. participated unofficially.
swap.text: This undeclared war between the U.S. and France during the French Revolutionary Wars saw various naval clashes in the Atlantic, stemming in part from French depredations on American shipping.
swap.clue: During this conflict, Thomas Truxton's Constellation captured the L'insurgente near Puerto Rico.

question.leadin: It was publicized by Samuel Brannan, who wrote of James Marshall's find at Sutter's Mill.
question.text: Name this event whose undertakers came to be known as the "forty-niners."
question.clue: The oldest continuously operating Taoist temple in America was built as part of this event, during which Lola Montez moved to the town of Grass Valley.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about education in antebellum America.
swap.text: This law required that each newly created township have land specially allocated for schools. Its other provisions included outlining the process for which territories became states.
swap.answerHtml: Northwest Ordinance [or the Northwest Ordinance of 1787; accept the Ordinance of 1787 or An Ordinance for the Government of the Territory of the United States, North-West of the River Ohio]
swap.clue: This law provided for three to five states to be established within its namesake territory once they reached a population of 60,000, the first of which became Ohio.

question.leadin: This woman met her long-lost brother Cameahwait during the event she is most associated with.
question.text: Name this Shoshone woman who, along with her husband Toussaint Charbonneau and son Pompey, accompanied one expedition after meeting them in the lands of the Mandan and Hidatsa tribes.
question.clue: After a group of explorers identified Cameahwait as this figure's long-lost brother, he gifted horses to those explorers.

swap.text: A political cartoon critical of this act shows a turtle snapping at a merchant, who exclaims "This cursed O-grab-me." It was later replaced by the Non-Intercourse Act.
swap.clue: This law, which sought to maintain English and French neutrality during the Napoleonic wars, was replaced by the Non-Intercourse Act and was depicted by Alexander Anderson as a snapping turtle.

question.leadin: During this event, Rear Admiral Cockburn reportedly ordered the destruction of all the "C" type in a newspaper building, so that his name could no longer be defamed.
question.text: Name this event led by Robert Ross that took place shortly after Ross's forces won the Battle of Bladensburg. During it, the Lansdowne portrait was legendarily saved by a woman.
question.answerHtml: The burning of Washington, D.C. [or the burning of the White House; or obvious equivalents]
question.clue: The dispersion of militiamen in the "Bladensburg races" allowed this event to occur, which was carried out by the occupying forces of George Cockburn and Robert Ross.

swap.leadin: A popular chengyu ("chung-eww") idiom sums up the 4th century as this many "barbarians" "throwing China into chaos" by founding the Sixteen Kingdoms during the Jin dynasty.
swap.text: Give this traditional number of dynasties that later arose alongside "ten kingdoms" between the Tang and Song. The "Celestial Masters" led a Daoist separatist movement named for this many "pecks of rice."
swap.answerHtml: five [or wǔ; accept Way of the Five Pecks of Rice or Wǔ Dǒu Mǐ Dào; accept Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms period or Wǔ dài shí guó; accept Five Barbarians or Wǔ Hú or Wǔ Hú luàn Huá]
swap.clue: The Roman king of this number was the first Etruscan one and was Tarquinius Priscus.

question.text: The vociferous prosecution of men like Callender for sedition led to the downfall of this Marylander, the only Supreme Court Justice to be impeached.
question.answerHtml: Samuel Chase [prompt on partial answer; do not accept “Salmon P. Chase”]
question.clue: This person mocked the defense as "a non sequitur" in a libel trial concerning the pamphlet The Prospect Before Us. This person told a grand jury in Baltimore that repeal of the Judiciary Act of 1801 was turning America into a "mobocracy."

swap.text: The plaintiff in this 1837 Supreme Court case tried to cite the Dartmouth case in complaining that the state of Massachusetts violated a 1785 charter that concerned traffic near the city of Boston.
swap.answer: Charles River Bridge v. Warren Bridge
swap.clue: The majority opinion in this 1837 case held that rights not specifically conferred could not be inferred from the language of a document.

question.leadin: Answer the following about what happened after the Battle of the Alamo.
question.text: This two-word term is used to describe the two months in early 1836 after the fall of the Alamo, when native Texans fled from their homes, hastily abandoning settlements like Washington-on-the-Brazos in fear of Santa Anna's army.
question.clue: Houston's victory at San Jacinto came after this desperate campaign, during which news of the massacres at the Alamo and Goliad caused the provisional government of Texas to flee from Santa Anna's advancing army.

swap.text: During the Barbary Wars, Thomas Jefferson tasked this man with overthrowing the government in Tripoli, in which capacity he fought the Battle of Derne. He shares his surname with the first governor of the New Haven Colony.

question.leadin: Name these Supreme Court decisions arising out of Virginia.
question.text: Arising out of a refusal by Virginia to abide by the decision in the Fairfax's Devisee case, this 1816 ruling said that the Judiciary Act of 1789 remained constitutional and Virginia had best abide by the Supreme Court's appellate jurisdiction or else.
question.clue: Joseph Story wrote the opinion in this case, which unanimously ruled that the Supreme Court could overrule the decisions of state courts. This case involved whether Virginia could void Loyalists' land grants after Jay's Treaty.

swap.leadin: Its namesake fled to Vermont after this movement was put down in February 1787.
swap.text: Name this anti-debt revolt in Massachusetts, which exposed certain weaknesses in the Articles of Confederation.
swap.clue: It was defeated at Petersham, allowing James Bowdoin to reassert control; less than a year later, its participants returned from exile in after new governor John Hancock pardoned those responsible for this event.
